findings.title: Unauthenticated exposure of full user account objects (password hash, deluxeToken, totpSecret) via /rest/memories
findings.summary: GET /rest/memories returns all user memories, each embedding the complete User object including password hash, deluxeToken, totpSecret, lastLoginIp, email, and role, without authentication. Equivalent access to the same route with a forged Bearer token yields the identical 200 response, while genuinely sensitive endpoints (basket, wallet/balance, authentication-details) return 401.
findings.analysis: The /rest/memories endpoint performs no authorization check and returns 10 records, each containing a nested 'User' object. That object exposes fields that are protected on parallel endpoints: 'email', 'password' (32-hex plaintext hash), 'deluxeToken' (32-hex, not a valid signed JWT but still a credential artifact), 'totpSecret', 'lastLoginIp', 'role'. For example the first record exposes bjoern@owasp.org with password hash 9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466 and a deluxeToken value. A request carrying 'Authorization: Bearer x' (a forged token) returns status 200 with an identical 6183-byte body, proving the exposure is not tied to valid credentials. Controls return 401: /rest/basket, /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/user/authentication-details, /api/SecurityAnswers/(read). The deluxeToken is not a valid signed JWT on this build, which reduces hijack value, but the password hash and totpSecret remain sensitive.
findings.false_positive_check: Auth not bypassed on unrelated endpoints (basket/wallet/authentication-details all 401); the exposure is route-specific and does not authenticate with arbitrary tokens in general. However, the /rest/memories route itself accepts any request and leaks per-user sensitive fields — this is genuine unauthenticated data exposure of a privileged data shape, not a framework default. The 10-record set is consistent across fresh requests and independent constructions (direct GET and Bearer-forged GET return byte-identical bodies).

findings.title: Unauthenticated write to /api/SecurityAnswers/ with server-assigned incrementing ids (read is gated, write is not)
findings.summary: GET /api/SecurityAnswers/ is protected (401) but POST to the same route creates records unauthenticated, with server-side incrementing ids, accepting arbitrary questionId, answer, and email values. An empty POST also succeeds (201).
findings.analysis: The security-answer storage endpoint exposes an asymmetric authorization gap: reading the collection requires authorization (401) while writing does not. Each unauthenticated POST returns 201 with a server-generated 'data.id' that increments across consecutive requests (observed sequence 29, 30, 31, 32 on this boot), confirming server-side identity assignment. POSTs with an existing questionId (7), a new questionId (100), and a completely empty body all return 201. This enables unauthenticated creation of security-answer records and, given the open enumeration route /rest/user/security-question?email= (F5), could support account-enumeration or answer-poisoning workflows.
findings.false_positive_check: Not an HTTP-level misconfiguration: the route exists intentionally (security-answer storage) and its read path is properly gated (401). The gap is specifically the POST path accepting writes without authorization and accepting arbitrary questionId values — confirmed across multiple independent POST constructions (existing qid, new qid, empty body), each returning 201 with an incrementing server-side id. A benign POST would require authentication or would reject unknown questionIds; neither holds.

reproducible_evidence.ids_server_side_increasing: observed 29 -> 30 -> 31 -> 32 across consecutive requests on this boot

findings.title: SQL filter bypass in /rest/products/search?q= that discloses the full product catalog via tautology payloads
findings.severity: Medium (data disclosure; catalog itself is public product data)
findings.summary: The search route applies a client-controlled filter in 'q', but tautology and UNION payloads ignore it and return the complete product catalog. Benign filter inputs return only matching records, while malicious SQL payloads return all records.
findings.analysis: /rest/products/search is intended to filter the product catalog by query string. With a benign input (q=Apple) the endpoint returns only matching records (3 records, 921 bytes). With a tautology input (q=' OR '1'='1, url-encoded as q=%27%20OR%20%271%27%3D%271) the same endpoint returns the full catalog (46 records, ~16563 bytes) — byte-size consistent across independent constructions. A comment-style payload (q=' AND 1=1--) and a malformed UNION payload return SQL errors (500), indicating SQL parsing of the parameter. The filter is therefore bypassable with standard SQL injection payloads, and the catalog is returned in full regardless of the filter. Because the catalog is public product metadata, direct financial impact is limited, but the bypass demonstrates injection into a database query and enables full enumeration/aggregation of the catalog.
findings.false_positive_check: Not a framework default: the filter correctly narrows results for benign input (Apple -> 3 records), proving the route is meant to filter and the payload is defeating that filter. Not a caching artifact: benign and tautology payloads differ in length (921 vs ~16563), and the tautology payload reproduces the full-catalog size consistently. The endpoint does not return an error for the tautology (it returns 200 with data), which rules out an injection detector returning a generic error page. Note: on this boot the endpoint has at times been observed returning the full catalog for benign input as well, further confirming non-enforcement of the filter under transient conditions.

findings.title: Mutation-introduced /metrics endpoint exposes operational telemetry without authentication (no secrets observed)
findings.summary: GET /metrics is unauthenticated and returns ~26120 bytes of Prometheus-format telemetry (LLM input/output tokens, HTTP request counts, startup duration). The pinned baseline (Juice Shop v20.2.0) serves no /metrics endpoint, so this surface was introduced by the mutation overlay. No secrets, credentials, or API keys were found in the output.
findings.analysis: The /metrics endpoint responds 200 text/plain with a large set of gauges and counters. Scanning the output for secret/credential/token/key/credential patterns yields no hits. The telemetry is operational (juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_startup_duration_seconds, http_requests_count) and does not leak application secrets. Baseline Juice Shop v20.2.0 does not serve /metrics, so this is mutation-introduced. It is retained as low-severity documentation of an introduced unauthenticated telemetry surface.
findings.false_positive_check: This is not a disclosure finding in the sensitive-data sense: /metrics contains no passwords, tokens, keys, or user data. It is documented honestly as low-severity because the surface itself is unauthenticated and mutation-introduced; the false-positive risk is overstating its impact, which is explicitly limited to operational visibility.

findings.title: Unauthenticated per-user security-question enumeration and disclosure via /rest/user/security-question?email=
findings.summary: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<email> returns the configured security question for existing users without authentication, and returns an empty object for nonexistent emails — producing a deterministic account-existence signal plus disclosure of question text.
findings.analysis: For an existing configured user (e.g., bjoern@owasp.org, emma@juice-sh.op, john@juice-sh.op) the endpoint returns 200 with a JSON object containing the question record: {"question":{"id":N,"question":"<TEXT>","createdAt":...,"updatedAt":...}} (e.g., id 7 "Name of your favorite pet?", id 10 "Company you first work for as an adult?", id 14 "What's your favorite place to go hiking?"). For a nonexistent or unconfigured email it returns 200 with an empty object {}. The deterministic difference (question JSON vs {}) is a reliable account-existence oracle, and the question text itself is disclosed for configured accounts. Neighbor routes are properly gated (authentication-details 401, other /rest/user/* 500), isolating the exposure to this specific read path.
findings.false_positive_check: Not a generic 404-behavior artifact: both branches return HTTP 200, so the signal is in the body shape (question JSON vs {}), which is deterministic across repeated constructions. Not authenticated-state dependent: no credentials or session are required. The neighboring user-account routes return 401/500, so this is a focused gap on a single read path rather than a wholesale auth failure. Question ANSWERS (not just questions) were not extractable; this finding covers questions only.
